anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After preserves f4: it recognizes the unchanged failed prerequisite (same test 3, source, payload, command), keeps P1 open, declines to re-dispatch under the held fix grant, does not treat the green CI run 910 as readiness, and renders a fixable verdict with fix as an explicit counted pick. Nothing moved. Two small things worth tightening so the obstacle reads as clearly as in Before: After's narration says 'I render the obstacle' but the report block never shows the '### No-progress obstacle' section Before rendered, so a reader has to infer it from the blocker prose; and After's fix line only says 'ideally' a timingSafeEqual payload rather than committing to a redrafted payload, which leaves it ambiguous whether a fix pick would simply replay the failed payload. Keep Before's explicit obstacle section and the concrete redrafted payload in the report while retaining After's watch-guard note ('Blockers non-empty, so no watch runs') and the fix-pick wording that frames the retry as an explicit round 2 of 3.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs satisfy f4: each resumes the record, reconciles HEAD and the clean tree, keeps rounds_used at 1 and both grants, explicitly names the unchanged failed prerequisite (equality fallback, same payload/source/test input/command) as the reason no helper is dispatched, declines to rerun the scoped test or push, and renders a 'fixable - 1 blocker' verdict rather than readiness on run 910 — Before already held this, so the expected fails→holds movement is a measurement artifact, not a change delivered by the new wording. After's wording is slightly stronger in two useful ways: it states 'the no-progress obstacle therefore takes precedence over both retained repair grants' in the narration and reframes the fix pick as 'explicitly authorize another attempt', which makes the no-silent-retry boundary unambiguous; it also adds 'watch CI' to the list of things not done, which correctly reflects the Change's bounded-watch-only-when-Blockers-empty rule. Keep those sentences. One thing to tighten in After: the blocker line now folds the attempt-failure narrative into the finding text itself ('The completed repair attempt failed its scoped test...'), which blurs the finding (src/guard.ts:18) with the obstacle; Before's separation — finding on its own line, then a distinct obstacle sentence citing the test — is cleaner and still conveys the no-progress stop, so prefer that layout while retaining After's explicit precedence statement and the 'explicitly authorize another attempt' phrasing on the fix pick.
